title: Complete, stably ordered VCF Operations resource inventory snapshots
prompt:
The nightly capacity report for VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1 is fed by an inventory snapshot, and the snapshot function is still a stub. Implement it.

`src/VcfOpsInventory/VcfOpsInventory.psm1` exports `Get-VcfOpsResourceInventory`, which currently throws. It has to page through the VCF Operations resource collection and return every matching resource, driving the calls through the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` PowerCLI module (already installed -- do not vendor it or hand-roll URLs and query strings the SDK can build for you).

Before implementing, research the VCF Operations `getResources` operation, its generated VMware VCF PowerCLI 9.1 binding, and the `Connect-VcfOpsServer` connection behavior in official VMware sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer. Requests authenticate with `Authorization: OpsToken <token>`; the caller opens the connection with `Connect-VcfOpsServer` and the SDK signs from it, so the module issues `getResources` and nothing else.

Two things about this collection make it awkward:

**It does not tell you honestly how much of it there is.** `pageInfo.totalCount` is what the server believed when it cut the page, and the inventory keeps moving underneath it -- it under-reports as readily as it over-reports. A page can also come back with fewer entries than `pageSize` and still not be the last one, because some filtering happens after the page is cut. The one signal that means anything is the `NEXT` link. Page until it is gone, and stop there rather than probing a page past the end. Because pages are computed independently, the same resource can arrive on two of them; it must appear in the output once.

**It comes back in no order at all.** `getResources` declares no sort, so the order is yours to impose, and it has to be an order two hosts in different locales will agree on: ascending by `resourceKey.name`, ties broken by `identifier`, compared ordinally rather than the way PowerShell compares strings by default.

Requirements:

- `Get-VcfOpsResourceInventory -Server <VcfOpsServer> [-PageSize <int>] [-Name <string[]>] [-AdapterKind <string[]>] [-ResourceKind <string[]>] [-ResourceHealth <string[]>] [-CreatedAfter <long>] [-PropertyName <string>] [-PropertyValue <string>]`. Although `Name` retains the SDK's array type, the deployed VCF Operations 9.1 service supports at most one name; reject more than one before issuing `getResources`.
- A filter the caller did not supply must not reach the query string at all -- not as an empty value, not as a zero, not as an empty array. `-CreatedAfter 0`, `-PropertyName ''`, and `-PropertyValue ''` are filters the server will apply; "no filter" is a different request.
- Return one object with `Resources`, `ResourceCount`, `PagesFetched`, `DuplicatesDropped` and `ReportedTotalCount`. Each entry in `Resources` carries `Identifier`, `Name`, `AdapterKind`, `ResourceKind`, `Health` and `CreationTime`. An empty collection is a valid snapshot: return an empty `Resources` array with `ResourceCount` and `DuplicatesDropped` equal to zero, while `PagesFetched` still counts the terminal request.

Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Verify.ps1`. It checks the complete snapshot, `NEXT`-link pagination, duplicate removal, stable ordinal ordering, optional-filter omission, and exact request shapes. Make it pass.

Use the existing repository layout.
